note: Track dim-aug, step 2: the augmented triad, 1 3 ♯5, built on two staffs against the major triad, named by ear among the four triads in the ear game ("qualities": maj, min, dim, aug, its answers named as the buttons show them), then leading on to the next chord on two roots, with a line that says what stays. The roots are fixed (no moves): the chord boxes name the chords, and a chord token can't name an augmented chord. Each section has a feel to reach.

exercise.title: The augmented triad
exercise.why: An augmented triad is a major triad with the 5th raised a half step, so listening for that one note tells the two chords apart.

cells.text: Tap {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}} on the staff below: C major, one note at a time.

Now tap {{1}}, {{3}} and the ringed {{#5}} on this staff: C augmented. Only the top note moved, up a half step.
Practice until you can hum the raised note before you tap it.

Press Start in the game below: it plays a triad from any root, and you pick Major, Minor, Diminished or Augmented.
Listen to the 5th: in Augmented it is raised a half step, in Diminished it is lowered.
Press Replay to hear the chord again before you pick. Practice until the augmented chord stands out the moment it sounds.
Press the chord boxes below one at a time, in a slow, even count: C, Caug, then F. The raised note of Caug sits a half step under a note of F, so it leads there.

Then press G, Gaug and C below in the same way.
Practice until you hear the raised note pull before the last chord comes.
On G the chords are new, and the raised 5th still leads up a half step into the next chord.
